name: The Louvre
tagline: The world's most visited museum, once a royal palace on the banks of the Seine.

rooms.name: The Italian Renaissance
rooms.description: The Denon wing's Salle des États and neighboring galleries, home to the Louvre's Italian masters.

artworks.title: Mona Lisa
artworks.description: The most visited single artwork in the world, famed for its atmospheric sfumato and the sitter's ambiguous half-smile. Leonardo carried it with him for years, reworking it until his death.
artworks.commonsFile: Mona Lisa, by Leonardo da Vinci, from C2RMF retouched.jpg

artworks.title: The Virgin and Child with Saint Anne
artworks.description: Left unfinished at Leonardo's death, this pyramidal composition of three generations shows his late mastery of soft transitions between light and shadow.

artworks.title: La Belle Jardinière
artworks.description: A Madonna and Child painted during Raphael's Florentine period, its title — "the beautiful gardener" — comes from the pastoral setting he gave the holy family.

artworks.title: The Wedding at Cana
artworks.description: The largest painting in the Louvre — a vast Venetian banquet scene depicting Christ's first miracle, crowded with over 130 figures in 16th-century dress.

artworks.title: The Fortune Teller
artworks.description: A gypsy fortune teller slips a ring from a young dandy's finger as she reads his palm — an early example of Caravaggio's street-level realism and psychological drama.

rooms.name: The Grand Gallery of French Painting
rooms.description: The Louvre's sweep of 18th- and 19th-century French history painting, hung floor to cornice.

artworks.title: Liberty Leading the People
artworks.description: Painted the same year it depicts, this allegory of the July Revolution shows a bare-breasted Liberty carrying the tricolor over the barricades and the dead.

artworks.title: The Raft of the Medusa
artworks.description: Survivors of a real 1816 shipwreck cling to a makeshift raft in this monumental, scandal-provoking indictment of naval incompetence and human desperation.

artworks.title: The Coronation of Napoleon
artworks.description: An enormous, meticulously documented record of Napoleon crowning Empress Josephine at Notre-Dame in 1804, painted as state propaganda by the era's leading Neoclassicist.

artworks.title: Oath of the Horatii
artworks.description: Three brothers swear to defend Rome as their father raises their swords — a Neoclassical manifesto of civic duty and stoic sacrifice that anticipated the Revolution.

rooms.name: The Hall of Antiquities
rooms.description: The ground-floor sculpture halls of the Sully and Denon wings, where Greco-Roman marble stands under skylights.

artworks.title: Venus de Milo
artworks.description: Discovered on the island of Milos in 1820, this armless Aphrodite has become the archetype of classical beauty despite — or because of — its missing limbs.

artworks.title: Winged Victory of Samothrace
artworks.description: The goddess Nike alights on a ship's prow, her drapery whipped by sea wind rendered in stone. Headless and armless, she still commands the top of the Daru staircase.

artworks.title: Borghese Gladiator
artworks.description: A fighter lunges mid-parry, every tendon carved in tension — a Hellenistic showpiece of anatomical bravura once owned by the Borghese family in Rome.

artworks.title: Diana of Versailles
artworks.artist: Roman copy after a Greek original (attrib. Leochares)
artworks.description: The huntress goddess strides forward with a stag at her side, a Roman marble copy of a lost Greek bronze once kept in the royal gardens at Versailles.

rooms.name: The Northern Cabinet
rooms.description: A quieter, intimately scaled room of Dutch and French court painting.

artworks.title: The Lacemaker
artworks.medium: Oil on canvas, mounted on panel
artworks.description: One of Vermeer's smallest works and among his most quietly intense — a young woman bent in total concentration over bobbin lace, thread rendered as flecks of pure pigment.

artworks.title: Gabrielle d'Estrées and One of Her Sisters
artworks.description: Two women sit in a bath, one pinching the other's nipple in a gesture read as announcing a royal pregnancy — one of the most enigmatic paintings in French art.

rooms.name: The Egyptian Crypt
rooms.description: Low-lit galleries of the Sully wing's Egyptian antiquities department, one of the largest collections outside Cairo.

artworks.title: Seated Scribe
artworks.medium: Painted limestone, rock crystal and copper inlay
artworks.description: An Old Kingdom scribe sits cross-legged with papyrus on his lap, his rock-crystal eyes giving the 4,000-year-old limestone an unsettlingly alert gaze.

artworks.title: Great Sphinx of Tanis
artworks.description: One of the largest sphinxes outside Egypt, this granite colossus guards the entrance to the Egyptian antiquities crypt much as it once guarded a temple at Tanis.
